newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil simplifies export finance terms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil simplifies export finance terms.

text.p: The Brazilian government has simplified some of the conditions for access to export financing, said Pedro Parente Executive Secretary of the Finance Ministry.
Parente told reporters the Council of Comercial Credit had modified some bureaucratic procedures for the granting of so-called Proex funds.
"This is part of a real war to increase Brazilian exports," Parente said.
- The Banco do Brasil will be able to issue export finance for up to $5.0 million without consulting the Council. Previously the limit was $1.0 million.
-- The Banco do Brasil will be able to authorize credit of up to 180 days without having to consult the Council.

-- The government will issue a decree allowing Proex funds destined to "equalization", basically subsidizing domestic interest rates to make them competitive with overseas rates, of up to 100 percent of the value of exports. Previously the limit was of 85 percent.
-- The government is studying a proposal to allow Proex equalization funds to be used to finance production of exports, and not just the exports themselves.

Parente said that the $1.0 billion in Proex funds had always been undersubscribed. He said that in the future if the changes led to greater demand the government would be prepared to plow money into the program.
